briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. We will now begin the climate briefing for September 14, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Global Climate Crisis Warnings and Impacts
sections.content: News continues to emerge, warning that global threats from climate change are deepening. Galapagos corals are sending a warning through 1,000 years of records that climate change is intensifying El Niño [5], and the 'climate crisis time bomb' warning that 80% of Himalayan glaciers could disappear by 2100 has been reignited [12]. This summer, unprecedented heatwaves occurred worldwide, causing glaciers to melt and mountains to collapse, making climate change a tangible reality [16, 118, 129, 139]. This has also emerged as a public health issue, leading to a surge in ambulance demand and affecting society as a whole [128, 143]. Furthermore, climate change is exacerbating the vulnerability of ecosystems and human societies by spreading diseases and pests that threaten crops and forests [123], and increasing fire risks in specific regions [124] [3, 131, 134, 135, 138].

sections.title: ⚠️ International Climate Policy Reversals and Calls for Strong Action
sections.content: Amidst the deepening climate crisis, international climate policy stands at a critical crossroads. Notably, former President Trump has labeled climate change a 'hoax,' stating his intention to abolish carbon regulations and revoke key regulations from the Biden administration era [1, 122, 125], thus showing movements that reverse global climate response efforts. In response, Prince William warned that 'incremental' actions alone are insufficient to halt climate change, urging urgent and strong measures [119, 121, 127, 130, 133, 137]. The UN Climate Chief also called for active action from the European Union (EU) ahead of COP31 [7]. In some regions, climate change is not being addressed as a major election issue [132], or the term 'climate change' is being removed from legislation [142], indicating deepening political indifference. This makes a practical system transition even more imperative [14, 115, 117, 126].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Spreading Domestic Carbon Neutrality Practices and Climate Adaptation Efforts
sections.content: Domestically, carbon neutrality practices and adaptation efforts to address the climate crisis are actively expanding. Numerous local governments, including Naju City, Gwanak-gu, and Gwangju Buk-gu, have been recognized for their achievements, receiving ministerial and chairman's awards as outstanding local governments nationwide for their citizen-participatory carbon neutrality policies [19, 22, 23, 24, 36, 37, 40, 41, 42, 43, 44, 45, 46, 47, 49, 51, 53, 56, 66, 72, 73, 77]. Voluntary citizen participation, such as Gwangmyeong City's 'Climate Volunteers' activities, is contributing to the spread of a carbon-neutral culture [26, 48, 52, 63, 69], and carbon neutrality education programs for future generations are also actively operating [25, 27, 29, 32, 34, 50, 57, 59, 65, 71, 81, 83]. Furthermore, corporations are also joining the efforts to combat climate change: GS E&C through future housing research [17], Coas by expanding carbon-neutral furniture using fire-damaged timber [38], and HD Hyundai by presenting a blueprint for carbon-neutral ships [79]. In addition, practical efforts are continuing in various other fields, including a paradigm shift in wildfire response [2], exploring climate-resilient agricultural models [6, 9, 10, 15], expanding people-centered transportation including for the mobility-impaired [35], and introducing reusable cups at highway rest areas [33, 55, 60] [4, 8, 13, 20, 28, 30, 31, 39, 54, 58, 61, 64, 68, 70, 74, 75, 76, 78, 80, 82, 84, 85, 114].

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition and Demands for Policy Improvement
sections.content: The transition to renewable energy is accelerating both domestically and internationally, emerging as a crucial means of energy security alongside its economic benefits. Renewable energy has proven its role as an 'economic breakwater' by curbing fossil fuel imports, stabilizing wholesale electricity prices [86], and saving 4.4 trillion won in fossil fuel electricity purchase costs over the past five months [91, 97, 107] [96]. The Jeju region is serving as a testbed for the national renewable energy market, having achieved a 24.3% share of renewable energy generation and expanding its 15-minute electricity market with VPP (Virtual Power Plant) and two-way bidding systems [92, 103]. The government has launched the 'Industrial Competitiveness Reinforcement Committee' to rebuild the solar power supply chain [102], and corporate investments and efforts continue, including iM Capital's expanded REC purchases [88, 93, 108], Gaon Cable's push into the new and renewable energy market [98], Korea East-West Power's large-scale project promotion [112], Samsung Electronics' presentation of high-efficiency EHS solutions [70], and Osstem Implant's increased use of renewable energy [105]. However, areas requiring policy improvement and in-depth discussion have also been raised, such as Seoul City's call for higher renewable energy targets [89, 94, 110], demands for electricity market improvements [99], and regional energy transition issues at the crossroads of carbon neutrality and carbon regression [101] [87, 90, 95, 100, 104, 106, 109, 111].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has highlighted the severity of the climate crisis, alongside the diverse efforts by the international community and domestically to overcome it. Strong and practical responses to climate change are more urgent than ever. This concludes today's climate briefing.
